clue.text: Order outline maps in decorative cover

indicators.note: to order things is to put them into a new sequence, so the following letters get rearranged

parts.note: thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone orders maps with outlines to be slipped inside an ornamental folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' reads like a command to buy something, but it signals the rearrangement of all thirteen letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is the everyday water-based paint used on interior walls, a coating applied for looks.

clue.text: Back final runner at Bow?

parts.note: the final part of something is its end
a horse is a runner in a race; at Bow, in Cockney East London, the h is dropped

explanation.surface: A punter backs the last horse in a race at Bow.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in the East End, home of Cockney speech, which drops the initial h, so a horse becomes 'orse.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a candidate or proposal is to give it your public support and approval.

clue.text: Surprise leading group

parts.note: a team that is leading is up
a set is a group of things belonging together

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words look like a description of a surprising frontrunner; split, they give two short words.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an upset is an unexpected result, a shock victory for the outsider.

clue.text: Son runs off — and runs off quickly!

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
a printer runs off copies, so it prints them

explanation.surface: A boy dashes away, and dashes very fast too.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'runs off' is the trick: first it means producing copies on a press, then it means dashing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a short burst of running at top speed, so whoever does that dashes away fast.

clue.text: Groan, perhaps, having a change of heart?

definitions.text: Groan, perhaps, having a change of heart?

parts.words: Groan, perhaps, having a change of heart?
parts.note: surface reading: a moan from someone who has changed their mind

parts.words: Groan, perhaps, having a change of heart?
parts.note: setter's reading: the word groan is a body part's name with its letters moved about, and a change of heart is a surgical operation

explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle the five letters of 'groan' and you get the musical or bodily word for a part of the body; a new heart is the most famous kind of surgical swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery replacing a failing heart with a donor's is the best-known example of moving body parts between people.

clue.text: Dad's outside initially mowing the grass

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: papa is a word for dad, plus the possessive s

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of mowing

explanation.surface: Father is out in the garden, starting to cut the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad must be read as papa, not pa, so that the possessive gives five letters to wrap around one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pampas grass is a tall ornamental plant with feathery plumes, native to the South American plains.

clue.text: Guard housed by private landlord

indicators.note: something housed is lodged inside a building, so one piece is lodged within another

parts.note: private feelings are inner ones
to keep something is to guard or protect it

explanation.surface: A security guard lives in a flat owned by a private landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier or a description of the landlord, but it supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a landlord is also the person who runs a pub or inn, serving drinks and letting rooms.

clue.text: May repackage heaters

definitions.note: a surname standing for the first name that goes with it

indicators.note: to repackage goods is to wrap and present them differently, so the letters come out in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone might give their radiators fresh boxes for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' sits at the start where it looks like the modal verb, but it is the surname of a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa May was the UK Conservative prime minister from 2016 to 2019, so her surname clues her forename.

clue.text: Poetry is modest but not empty when read aloud

definitions.note: a mass noun for a plural answer

indicators.note: 'but not' means except for, so certain letters are left out

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reading something out turns it into spoken sound, so the word's sound is spelt out as letters

parts.note: said aloud, the two letters M and T sound like the word empty

explanation.surface: A remark that verse is humble without being vacuous.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'empty' is the letters M and T; strip those two from the six-letter word and four remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyrical poems addressed to a subject, so a collection of them is a body of verse.

clue.text: Arranged for Heath to follow strict diet

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed at the end

parts.note: a regimen is a prescribed, disciplined course of diet or exercise
Ted Heath was the UK Conservative prime minister of 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A doctor has set up an austere eating plan for the former prime minister Edward Heath.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath is not heathland but Edward 'Ted' Heath, a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Regimented describes things organised in strict, orderly ranks, like soldiers in a regiment.

clue.text: Greek islander hiding in secret annexe

indicators.note: something hiding inside is concealed within the words that follow

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A man from a Greek island is lying low in a concealed back room.
explanation.walkthrough: The secret annexe recalls Anne Frank's hiding place, which makes the hiding sound literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest Greek island, so someone born or living there is from a Greek island.

clue.text: Tidied up after newspaper head has dined with editor

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: opening letter of newspaper
someone who has dined has eaten
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone cleared up after the paper's boss had a meal with an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper head' sounds like the paper's chief, but it is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To neaten something is to make it tidy and orderly, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: It's trendy to work around canines?

definitions.text: It's trendy to work around canines?

indicators.note: to work something is to knead and shape it, so the letters get reshaped

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims it is fashionable to do jobs involving dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Canines suggest dogs, but they are also the pointed teeth beside the incisors; the whole clue describes the profession while its first words are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental work covers all the teeth, including the pointed canine teeth, which a profession of tooth doctors treats.

clue.text: Island's border crossing showing native loyalty

indicators.note: to cross something can mean to straddle it from side to side, so one piece spans another

parts.note: a trim is a decorative edging or border
Bali is an Indonesian island, plus the possessive s

explanation.surface: Islanders passing through a frontier checkpoint display allegiance to their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border crossing' reads as a frontier post, but the border is the outer piece that does the crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribalism is strong allegiance to one's own tribe or group, the loyalty of a people to their kin.

clue.text: Wonderful father returns to Samoan capital

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as the letter I
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A beloved dad travels home to the Pacific island capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 meaning excellent is a crossword staple, with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Apia is the capital city of Samoa, an island nation in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Revolutionary Irishman's correspondence

indicators.note: a revolution is a full turn, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: Liam is a common Irish man's name

explanation.surface: Letters written by an Irish rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary Irishman' calls up a nationalist rebel, but it only signals turning a name round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail is letters and parcels sent by post, which is the stuff of correspondence.

clue.text: Menu's starter — a large fat duck

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: opening letter of menu
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A restaurant's first course is a big, greasy duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The menu, starter and fat duck all build a dinner scene, but 'starter' only picks one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the commonest wild duck, the green-headed drake familiar from ponds.

clue.text: Typically too old to absorb sodium

indicators.note: to absorb something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: over age means past the age limit
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: An observation that elderly people usually cannot take in enough salt.
explanation.walkthrough: Sodium's symbol comes from its Latin name natrium.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something happens on average means it is what usually or normally occurs.

clue.text: Forces' sweetheart is a hundred at heart — that shows guts

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so this goes in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: Vera Lynn, the wartime singer, was known as the Forces' Sweetheart
taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A wartime singer is said to be brave at heart, and her courage is on display.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Vera Lynn sang to British troops in the Second World War and earned the nickname Forces' Sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscera are the internal organs of the body, especially those in the abdomen, the guts.

clue.text: Budget events holding pay back

indicators.note: to hold something is to contain it, so the answer sits inside these words

parts.note: runs from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Annual Budget announcements that keep wages from rising.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Budget is the Chancellor's yearly statement on taxes and spending, which suits talk of pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay someone back is to take revenge, to settle the score with them.

clue.text: Transfer Anglo-Saxon notice

parts.note: AS is the abbreviation for Anglo-Saxon
a sign is a posted notice

explanation.surface: An Old English document announcing a handover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' could be a verb meaning spot, but here it is the noun, a posted sign.
explanation.definitionFit: In law to assign a right or property is to formally hand it over to someone else.

clue.text: Makes plain consomme, perhaps, having nothing to lose

indicators.note: losing something means no longer having it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: consommé is an example of a thin, clear broth
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cook simplifies a broth to the point where it has nothing left to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain consomme' reads as one phrase, but 'Makes plain' is the definition and 'perhaps' marks consomme as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a confusion is to explain it and make it understandable.

clue.text: Extraordinary feat in outskirts of Surrey gets protection

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another
the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Surrey

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remarkable achievement in the suburbs of Surrey earns someone a guard.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London, whose outskirts read naturally as suburbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety is the state of being protected from harm or danger, a shelter from risk.

clue.text: Fuming, missing medium shaped moulds?

indicators.note: to shape something is to mould it into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
something missing is absent, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: An angry artist without a mid-sized tool makes casting moulds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moulds' looks like a verb or casting forms after 'shaped', but it is the noun for growths.
explanation.definitionFit: Moulds are a kind of fungus, growing as furry patches on damp walls and old food.

clue.text: Shallow end removed — it had to help?

indicators.note: taking away the end means cutting off the last letter

parts.note: facile means superficial or shallow
taken as written
to have a meal is to eat, so had can be ate

explanation.surface: The shallow end of a pool was taken out, perhaps to make things easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shallow end' suggests a swimming pool, but 'end removed' docks the last letter of the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To facilitate is to make a process easier, so it means to assist or aid.

clue.text: Vote against including Victory in the fleet

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a nay is a vote against
V is the abbreviation for victory

explanation.surface: Sailors oppose bringing HMS Victory back into service.
explanation.walkthrough: Victory evokes Nelson's flagship, but here it is just the abbreviation V.
explanation.definitionFit: A navy is a country's sea force, its whole body of warships and sailors.

clue.text: Sinner and saint helping at protest

parts.note: a demon is an evil spirit, a wrongdoer
ST is the standard abbreviation for saint
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer and a holy figure are lending a hand at a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb about assisting, but it is a noun meaning a share of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a public march or rally voicing opposition, so it is a form of public dissent.
